classification: Source inspiration / source-credited native media lifecycle adaptation
behavior: Retain the existing native video, its source/poster/loop/mute/controls and caller events.
Admit playback only for a visible host and video, a visible document and a permitted motion target. Freeze Canvas/export/thumbnail/reduced motion.
Retain native manual Pause across viewport, video and host replacement; release observers/listeners and prevent late Play from escaping suspension.
Create no media element, decoder, canvas, timer or animation loop.
Recheck settled CSS transition/animation paint through scoped completion events; no polling or extra clock.

The explicit manual override waits for an admitted native Play before starting media; hidden Play is rejected, previous unpaused playback may resume on viewport return, and manual Pause remains latched.
integrationBoundary: The native Framer Video forwards a Playing control but its runtime playing prop and HTMLElement ref bridge have not been observed.

Keep serialized Playing true on the two existing Mac Moss autoplay loops while testing their host bridge; live automatic mode fails open to caller playback if no host is forwarded. New manual studies instead retain serialized Playing false and require an available native Play control.
A native-like React fixture is not proof of actual native Framer offscreen suspension or idle editor behavior.
Manual mode needs a native Play affordance while Playing=false; a player that mounts its sole affordance only when Playing=true cannot bootstrap this mode.
